speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort; to help me narrow down the cause, how long have these symptoms been occurring?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Infectious Colitis (likely Campylobacter or similar bacterial etiology) secondary to recent camping exposure. The presentation of chronic diarrhea, urgency, mucus, tenesmus (incomplete evacuation), and relief with defecation following a specific exposure event in a 31-year-old female is highly suggestive of an infectious colitis rather than a primary inflammatory bowel disease like IBD.

I will not order additional tests as the clinical picture is sufficient for this diagnosis based on the history provided.
